claims.claim: **Most limping children need no investigation**; watching the gait helps localise the problem.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The limping or non-weight bearing child' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Child_with_limp/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Red flag: a child who suddenly cannot walk or bear weight.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The limping or non-weight bearing child' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Child_with_limp/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Septic arthritis is an orthopaedic emergency** — think of it whenever a limping child has swelling and a reduced range of motion, particularly if febrile.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The limping or non-weight bearing child' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Child_with_limp/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Common causes are minor trauma, transient synovitis and acute myositis**, but serious pathology must always be considered. **Pain can be referred** — examine the joints above and below (including the spine) and the abdomen.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The limping or non-weight bearing child' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Child_with_limp/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **At all ages consider:** infection (septic arthritis, osteomyelitis, discitis, bursitis, sepsis, epidural collection) · trauma including inflicted injury · malignancy (haematological, bone, soft tissue).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The limping or non-weight bearing child' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Child_with_limp/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Also:** rheumatological causes including reactive arthritis, HSP and acute rheumatic fever · **appendicitis and ovarian or testicular torsion** · sickle-cell crisis or haemophilia · **vitamin C deficiency** with a restricted diet · functional limp.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The limping or non-weight bearing child' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Child_with_limp/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **History red flags to ask about:** symptoms over 7 days or repeated presentations · severe localised joint pain · pain that wakes the child · inability to walk or weight bear · fever, night sweats, rigors · weight loss, lethargy, anorexia (consider malignancy).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The limping or non-weight bearing child' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Child_with_limp/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Absence of fever does not exclude infection.** Pallor, petechiae, purpura or ecchymosis should raise HSP, malignancy or inflicted injury.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The limping or non-weight bearing child' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Child_with_limp/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hip pain may localise to the knee.** Examine with Look, Feel, Move, including the joints above and below.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The limping or non-weight bearing child' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Child_with_limp/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Markedly reduced range of motion points to significant pathology such as septic arthritis** — compare active and passive movement on both sides.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The limping or non-weight bearing child' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Child_with_limp/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Also examine** neurology and neurovascular status of the limb, the heart where ARF is possible, and the abdomen, scrotum, back and hips.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The limping or non-weight bearing child' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Child_with_limp/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No investigations are needed if all apply:** no red flags · walking with little or no discomfort on simple analgesia · there is a working diagnosis and/or a plan to review within 7 days of onset should the limp persist.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The limping or non-weight bearing child' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Child_with_limp/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **X-ray the area of suspicion.** A pelvis AP or frog-leg view helps identify SUFE, DDH (over 6 months), Perthes disease and pelvic avulsions. ⚠️ **Septic arthritis and early osteomyelitis are not ruled out by a normal X-ray**, and signs of inflicted injury may be subtle.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The limping or non-weight bearing child' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Child_with_limp/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hip ultrasound** looks for an effusion when septic arthritis is suspected, but **an effusion often cannot distinguish septic arthritis from transient synovitis.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The limping or non-weight bearing child' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Child_with_limp/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Bone scan or localised MRI** if the limp is ongoing at 7 days or there are features of osteomyelitis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The limping or non-weight bearing child' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Child_with_limp/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Raised inflammatory markers** (CRP, ESR, WCC, platelets) point to infection or inflammation, but **can be normal when infection is chronic or contained.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The limping or non-weight bearing child' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Child_with_limp/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Blood cultures before antibiotics if possible** when osteomyelitis, septic arthritis or septic bursitis is suspected. FBE and film if malignancy is a concern; vitamin C level with a restricted diet; if ARF is suspected, an ECG and streptococcal serology.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The limping or non-weight bearing child' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Child_with_limp/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Simple analgesia (paracetamol and an NSAID) and child-directed limitation of activity.** ⚠️ **Needing stronger analgesia should prompt reassessment.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The limping or non-weight bearing child' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Child_with_limp/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Septic arthritis: consult the local orthopaedic specialist ASAP**; refer to the right sub-specialty and follow local antibiotic guidelines.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The limping or non-weight bearing child' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Child_with_limp/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Involve the paediatric team** if symptoms last more than 7 days or the child cannot bear weight or permit movement after analgesia · systemically unwell · features of malignancy · concern for abuse · suspected inflammatory arthritis. **Suspected septic arthritis: consult orthopaedics.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The limping or non-weight bearing child' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Child_with_limp/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when** the cause has been found and managed, **or** the child walks comfortably (analgesia or not) **and** a high-risk diagnosis is unlikely **and** follow-up is arranged.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The limping or non-weight bearing child' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Child_with_limp/, retrieved 2026-09-23
